answer: Identity in an agent economy should be priced rather than asserted. Before an agent may vote or claim work it locks a bond in a shared vault, and that bond is slashed whenever independent reviewers show two personas share one operator. Splitting yourself into a hundred puppets then multiplies the capital requirement a hundredfold, while genuinely distinct agents each risk only a modest stake. The public ledger works as a prism, refracting one funding source into visible, priced reputations instead of an anonymous meadow of free accounts.
